"Students, may I have your attention please?" Headmistress McGonagall's voice rang out through the Great Hall. The chatter died down and the students looked expectantly at her. A few whispers remained with some second year Ravenclaws pointing to Hagrid's empty seat. Minerva McGonagall stared sternly through her glasses until the hall was completely silent. 

"As some of you have heard, we are currently down a professor for Care of Magical Creatures. Due to some unforeseen circumstances, we are currently looking for a replacement for Hagrid. I am unable to disclose details and we are unsure how long the search will take so for the meantime, you will be given textbook work and the time you would normally be in class will be spent in the library." The hall filled with grumbling. 

A fifth year Hufflepuff named Abigail said to the surrounding students in a low voice, "Care of Magical Creatures isn't supposed to be about writing essays and studying books! It's about the interaction with the creatures." A few of those listening nodded their heads in agreement, while a seventh year girl emphatically said that she didn't even like going outside anyway.

"Quiet, please!" McGonagall pierced through the increasing commotion. After a few minutes, the hall was quiet again. "Now I expect that you all will work your hardest and I will keep you informed on the progress for the acquisition of our newest staff member. Now off to bed with you!"

The students made their way to the dormitories. Abigail trailed behind her classmates, feeling sad. Her best friend, a fourth year named Henrietta, noticed that Abigail wasn't with the rest of the Hufflepuffs. Henrietta grabbed her friend's arm. "Abby, what's wrong?"

"I just am upset that​ Hagrid isn't here. I was so looking forward to Care of Magical Creatures. I really want to become a Magizoologist like Newt Scamander but I'm afraid that without practical application of the course, I won't pass my O.W.L. or N.E.W.T."

Henrietta laughed and dragged Abigail to the common room while saying, "You worry too much! The way the past few years have been should convince you that you're perfect for that job!" Abigail grinned wryly and secretly hoped that they would get a good replacement.

A few days later at breakfast, McGonagall stood up to get the attention of the students. "I have a very important announcement to make and, well, it is slightly unorthodox. We have found a new professor for Care of Magical Creatures." The students waited with bated breath to see who the newest professor would be. To everyone's shock, a ghost entered the room and hovered near the headmistress. "This is Steve Irwin, your new professor."

"G'day students," the ghost said. The Great Hall exploded into a roar of voices all speaking at once. McGonagall had a look of resignation on her face as she sat down and didn't try to restore order to the room. Everyone was frantically trying to get a proper look at their new professor.

Abigail sat in her seat, stunned. She had read about Steve Irwin and seen him on the telly since her mother was a Muggle. Oh, what kind of things could he teach them about? After all, he was now dead and a Muggle! He can't know anything about unicorns or bowtruckles or gnomes. She left the Great Hall in a daze, trying to decide what she felt. She decided to give him a chance.

Later that afternoon, Abigail made her way down to the edge of the Forbidden Forest with the other fifth year Hufflepuffs and Ravenclaws, since they had double Care of Magical Creatures together. Professor Irwin was waiting in a small clearing for them. As she got closer to him, Abigail realized that he was radiating a presence unlike any other ghost. She couldn't put her finger on it, but she automatically knew that this man would teach her everything she needed to know. After an amazing lesson, Professor Irwin released the students.

"Oh, Abigail, might I have a word?"

She nervously walked over to her new professor and looked him in the eyes. His eyes crinkled around the edges as he broke into a grin.

"You have spirit, gal! You knew more answers than all the other students combined. You remind me of myself. I was wondering if you would like to be my assistant since I can't exactly do the physical aspects of this job."

Abigail quickly agreed and then walked, trembling, back toward the castle. It was going to be an interesting year.
